newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - Ballot fever hits French debt derivatives.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Ballot fever hits French debt derivatives.

text.p: Out of the blue, France is grappling with political uncertainty, giving a boost to the French debt derivatives market.
Implied volatility of options on Pibor futures traded on MATIF have shot higher as the futures have stumbled. And brokers see scope for even bigger premiums on French credit options.

"The market feels fairly nervous," said Rhys Rogers, broker at Trifutures in Paris. "We'll probably see a bounce (in the futures), but short-term it's probably right to be short the market in terms of directions."
He added, "It's probably early to start thinking about selling vols."

The entire French curve has weakened on speculation President Jacques Chirac will announce a snap election for late May or early June, with the impact being felt hardest at the short end. Chirac is due to make an address at 1800 GMT.
Brokers quoted June Pibor options volatility at 37 percent, up sharply from 24 percent on Friday. Implied volatility has more than tripled in the last week according to MATIF data.
Brokers said few players had been long of volatility ahead of the latest bout of political uncertainty.

"What we're seeing driving the market is quite fresh stuff," Rogers said. Throughout the first quarter of this year volatility has been sold down from higher levels and that liquidation has largely been completed, he said.
"I don't think anyone was particularly long vol going into this," Rogers said.
Andy Ash, derivatives analyst at Monument Derivatives in London, said big market moves were brewing.

"The volumes are abysmally low which is often a prelude to a major move," he said. While French markets were being helped by recent strength in U.S. bonds they were undermined by the domestic situation.
"Sooner or later one will win and we think it will happen within a week," Ash said.
Rogers at Trifutures said volume in the futures was strong, although less so in the options. Even so, it was busier than it had been in some time.
At 1420 GMT, June Pibor futures were at 96.29, down 20 basis points on the day and just above the day's lows. June notionnel futures were 0.48 lower at 128.24.
